purpose: Retarget Mii Swordfighter Hero Spin (up-B) motions onto elight c07 by bone-name intersection, replacing the recipient slots' own vanilla clips. No animation name is introduced and no carrier is repointed: every slot written already exists in the base install.

evidence.recipient_slot_metadata: references/mythra_ftilt/elight_body_motion_list.yml (elight body c00; the dump's elight c07 and c00 motion_list.bin are byte-identical)

binding_semantics: Recipient animation node order is alphabetical, skeleton order is hierarchical, so transform binding is by node name, not index.

visibility_group.rationale: The donor carries Transform + Visibility only, and its visibility names the Mii's meshes, so both recipient groups are replaced from the recipient's own default standing motion. That clip is constant in both groups, which is what allows it to be resized to a clip of any length without inventing values.
visibility_group.rejected_alternative: The recipient's own up-B family (d02specialhi*, layout dee56b0400c5, 34 visibility nodes) matches the slot being written, but it animates 2 of those visibility tracks (eflame_Mouth_Heavyattack, eflame_Mouth_Talk) and 2 material tracks (CustomVector31 on EyeL and EyeR), so it cannot be retimed onto a donor clip of a different length without inventing values. Those two animated recipient tracks are therefore not reproduced; the meshes they drive hold the constant values the recipient's own idle also uses. Recorded as a limitation, not asserted away.

patches.why: loop: true. The donor slot special_air_hi1_loop carries it, the recipient slot does not, and the ported Loop status never tests MotionModule::is_end(), so a six-frame clip without it plays once and holds its final frame.
cancel_frame: 45, the donor value. The recipient slot is 0, so the interrupt window the donor End phase has would be lost.

not_applied_deliberately.field: xlu_start / xlu_end on special_hi_start and special_air_hi_start
not_applied_deliberately.reason: PLAN.md section 12 records the donor fading the model in over frames 5 to 13 and the recipient slots at 0/0. That is a design decision for the port, not one of the two measured mismatches this tool was asked to fix, so it is recorded here and left alone rather than decided silently.

open_items: The recipient's esword motion list has no up-B entries, so no sword clip is written; how the Aegis sword behaves during the spin is a Switch observation, not something the donor can answer.
The two animated recipient visibility tracks and two animated material tracks of the vanilla up-B family are not reproduced; see visibility_group.rejected_alternative.
